::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** July 11th [1889]  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS  Mrs Julia Birley/2
:::

My dear [Mr Dean](people/person_244.qmd)

Please tell me if I am wrong in objecting to have the 1st Psalm set down wholly as Maccabean? It is in [Mr Rodwell](people/person_2386.qmd)’s comments on the Psalms in his new [Newbery Magazine](organizations/other_89.qmd)[^1] which I have had to notice.  There was no previous explanation why <u>any</u> Psalms should be said to be Maccabean (though of course I know it is said of more obvious ones, though I don’t believe it)  And the reason was odd, that the 1st Psalm seemed to belong to a time when everybody was to study the law, not only rulers as in Deut XVI and Joshua I-  Just as if the 6th of Deuteronomy did not enforce it upon everybody!  I know the 1st Psalm is said not to be David’s but I never saw it attributed to anyone later than Ezra.  I don’t want to be too narrow and ignorant of criticism but I don’t find this in [Wordsworth](other_books/otherbook_804.qmd) or [Thrupp](other_books/otherbook_928.qmd) and I have not [Browne](other_books/otherbook_1084.qmd).

Surely I need not believe in direct inspiration between Malachi and St Matthew.

I should like to be discussing it in the porch at the Mead[^2]

yours affectionately
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: The *Newbery House Magazine* was new in 1889, and Rodwell's series of articles on the Psalms were advertised in the first issue, but CMY does not seem to have mentioned them in *MP*.
[^2]: The Mead, Wantage, was a house where William Butler used to stay in Wantage after he ceased to be vicar and became successively (1877) canon of Worcester and (1885) Dean of Lincoln.
